1	# WP-001: Add Audit Logging for Credential Mutations
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Address all actionable deferred items from the multi-credential-support synthesis — this plan removes dead code, hardens security, persists credential badge state, improves GUI accessibility, adds audit logging, fills test coverage gaps, and fixes a test infrastructure hang.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Wire `errorLogManager` into the credential route handlers and add structured audit log entries for all credential mutation operations (create, update, delete, assign, clear) using the existing `ErrorLogManager` infrastructure with `Source: 'credential-audit'`.
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `src/server/routes/config.ts` — add `errorLogManager?: ErrorLogManager` to `ConfigRoutesOptions`; add audit log calls in PUT and DELETE credential handlers
    14	- `src/server/routes/repositories.ts` — add `errorLogManager?: ErrorLogManager` as a fourth parameter to `registerRepositoryRoutes()`; add audit log call in PUT credential handler
    15	- `src/server/index.ts` — update both call sites to pass `errorLogManager`
    16	- `src/server/__tests__/routes/config.test.ts` — add audit logging test cases
    17	- `src/server/__tests__/routes/repositories.test.ts` — add audit logging test cases
    18	
    19	## Deliverables
    20	
    21	- `errorLogManager` wired into `ConfigRoutesOptions` and `registerRepositoryRoutes()` parameter list
    22	- `startServer()` call sites updated to pass `errorLogManager`
    23	- Audit log entry on credential create/update (PUT /api/config/credentials)
    24	- Audit log entry on credential delete (DELETE /api/config/credentials/:id)
    25	- Audit log entry on credential assign/clear (PUT /api/repositories/:id/credential)
    26	- All audit entries use `Source: 'credential-audit'`, `Severity: 'warning'`, and include `id`, `label`, `host` but never `token`
    27	- Test cases verifying audit log entries for each mutation type and verifying token absence
    28	
    29	## Dependencies
    30	
    31	- None
    32	
    33	## Acceptance Criteria
    34	
    35	1. `errorLogManager` is available in both `config.ts` and `repositories.ts` route handler scope via the updated interfaces and call sites.
    36	2. Credential create, update, and delete operations produce audit log entries with `Source: 'credential-audit'` and appropriate `Operation` values (`create-credential`, `update-credential`, `delete-credential`).
    37	3. Credential assign and clear operations produce audit log entries with `Source: 'credential-audit'` and `Operation` values (`assign-credential`, `clear-credential`).
    38	4. No audit log message contains a credential token value.
    39	5. All new and existing route tests pass.
    40	
    41	## Active Pipeline Stages
    42	
    43	`implementation` → `qa` → `security-audit` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    44	
    45	## Estimated Complexity
    46	
    47	High
    48	
    49	## Rationale
    50	
    51	Using `ErrorLogManager` with `Source: 'credential-audit'` rather than a new `AuditLogManager` — the existing infrastructure is proven, has FIFO eviction, filtering by source, and a REST API + GUI view. A dedicated audit logger is not justified until the tool has user authentication (which it does not — localhost-only tool).
    52	
    53	## Rejected Approaches
    54	
    55	- **New `AuditLogManager` class:** Rejected because it adds unjustified complexity for a localhost tool. The existing `ErrorLogManager` already has REST API and GUI integration.
    56	- **Structured log file:** Rejected because it lacks the REST API and GUI integration that `ErrorLogManager` provides out of the box.
    57	- **Console-only logging:** Rejected because console output is ephemeral and not queryable through the GUI.
    58	
    59	## Notes
    60	
    61	The wiring of `errorLogManager` into route handlers (Step 5.0) is a prerequisite for the audit logging logic. Both are bundled here because the wiring alone has no user-visible deliverable. `Severity: 'warning'` is used because `'warning'` is the closest match for informational audit entries — the existing severity enum only has `'error' | 'warning'`. The code snippet in the plan uses `isUpdate` and `savedEntry` which do not exist by name in the current handler — `isUpdate` maps to `existingIndex !== -1` and `savedEntry` refers to the entry object just written into `appConfig.gitCredentials`. Touches `src/server/routes/config.ts` (also touched by WP-004, WP-005) and `src/server/routes/repositories.ts` (also touched by WP-008).
